newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises on prompt, boosted by flex buying.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises on prompt, boosted by flex buying.

text.p: The U.K. spot natural gas market saw a focus on short term gas on Tuesday, especially for within-day and day-ahead supply, traders and brokers said.

The burst of activity on the short term market was largely caused by the cold weather over the bank holiday weekend and on Tuesday, which caused a system buy on the flexibility mechanism on Tuesday morning, they added.

The flexibility mechanism bought at up to 0.4981 pence a kiloWatt hour (kWh), or around 14.60 pence a therm on Tuesday, following a purchase at higher prices on Monday. This became a "reference price" against which traders looked to do within-day trade.

One potential seller reported seeing this level and offering within-day gas at 14.50 pence as a result, but buyers were not willing to come so high. Instead, the largest buyer in this market purchased a total of 700,000 therms in three separate trades, all at 14.30 pence a therm.

The day ahead market was also busy because of cold weather and presumed increased demand. Although the temperature on Wednesday is set to rise slightly from Tuesday's level, it is still set to be well below the seasonal normal level. Transco forecasts demand on Wednesday at 240 mcm, or 56 percent of peak day demand, compared with a Tuesday forecast of 238 mcm, also 56 percent of peak demand.
The temperature is forecast for Wednesday at 6.9 Celsius, above Tuesday's 4.8 Celsius but still well below the seasonal normal 12.0 Celsius.

For most of the morning and early afternoon the spot market concentrated on the short term with the forward curve barely getting talked. But in later trade there was some interest seen for Q1 98, at the top end of the existing range with at least three trades done at or near 16.30 pence a therm. There was also said to be good buying interest for the gas year starting in October 1997, with bids reported coming above 13.00 pence a therm, although no deals were confirmed done.

One trader was surprised by the increase in tone for prices later in the year. "The forward curve did nothing for most of the day but then crept up a bit," he said. "The prompt market gave a slightly firmer tone to the whole thing," he added, although there appeared to be no connection between the two.
The IPE futures market saw a disappointing start to the week, with only 20 lots done in three separate trades, all off from Friday's closing levels, in contrast to the physical market.
